messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: P1 — elevated 5xx rate observed for /v1/generate (inference-runner) in us-west-2. Current alert: 12% 5xx, error spike started ~ 5m ago. Paging on-call.

priya.k: ack — I'm oncall. Jumping in now. Annotating timeline. ETA 2m to post first findings.

emily: seeing same on dashboards. p95 latency up from 220ms -> 1.1s for that route. Conservatively marking customer-impacting.

marco.s: pulling logs/querying traces. quick query against logs:```
# ad-hoc logs query (observability)
service:inference-runner | where status >= 500 and time > now()-10m | count() by error_message | sort by count desc
```

marco.s: top error text: "kv-cache write timeout" (~480 events), second is "redis timeout" (~200 events).

nate: tagging infra — could be KV flush fallback hitting disk. Are we seeing increased IO or pod restarts?

emily: no pod restarts in the last 10m. Node CPU normal. I do see a spike in pod OOM_kill events 06:12 -> 06:15 but only 2 restarts.

liz: quick note — we changed log sampling to 10% for inference-runner on 1764220000 (cost optimization). That might explain why traces are sparse. If critical, we should momentarily raise to 100% to get full error payloads.

priya.k: do it. Increase sampling to 100% in us-west-2 for inference-runner. Also enable debug-level for the affected deployment for 15m.

ops-bot: executed: `config apply sampling=inference-runner us-west-2=100%` — change started.

marco.s: re-running query after sampling change:```
# re-run after sampling ramp
service:inference-runner | where status >= 500 and time > now()-5m | top 20 error_message, host
```

marco.s: new details — many errors include "OOM during kv-cache flush" on hosts i-0fa3 and i-0b7c. Also see elevated redis latency: 120-250ms in the same window.

nate: hypothesis 1: memory pressure on inference containers during KV flush leading to OOM and 5xx. Hypothesis 2: a transient upstream redis latency cascade causing timeouts which then trigger heavy retry/flush churn.

priya.k: timeline so far:
- ~1764309800: first metric deviation detected by alerting
- 1764309876: alert page (this thread)
- 1764309900: initial query shows 5xx surge, top error kv-cache write timeout
- 1764309945: sampling increased to 100% and debug enabled
- 1764309980: more detailed logs reveal OOMs and redis latency spikes

emily: quick check on dashboards — noticed that the "inference-runner latency" dashboard was using `avg` instead of `p95` for the widget that drives our alarm. I corrected the widget (now p95) to avoid noisy thresholds. That was a pre-existing observability bug.

marco.s: sharing a snippet of the problematic stacktrace (sanitized):```
2026-03-14T06:13:14Z ERROR kv_cache.go:412 - kv flush failed: write timeout after 30s | mem_used=78% | heap_alloc=1.8GB
2026-03-14T06:13:15Z ERROR redis_client.go:87 - write to redis timed out: context deadline exceeded (120ms)
```

liz: FYI — last config change to kv-flush concurrency was rolled 2d ago to increase throughput. Could be related (concurrency bump -> more memory pressure).

priya.k: mitigation plan executed now:
- scale inference-runner replicas +2 in us-west-2 (to spread KV flushes)
- lower kv-flush concurrency from 8 -> 4 via runtime flag
- roll back recent kv-flush concurrency change (if ramping)
- temporary model-fallback: route traffic to smaller quantized variant to reduce memory pressure

ops-bot: scaling: `kubectl scale deployment/inference-runner --replicas=12 -n prod-us-west-2` — done.

nate: lowered kv flush concurrency via feature-flag service (applied): `KV_FLUSH_CONCURRENCY=4` — change propagated.

emily: routed 20% traffic to quantized variant as immediate fallback. Watching error rate and latency.

~5m after mitigations

marco.s: error rate dropping — 5xx from 12% -> 3.2%. Redis latency back to baseline ~30ms. OOM events stop.

priya.k: handoff plan — I'm handing to nate for the next 40m to watch for recurrence and start RCA write-up. Marking incident as in-mitigation. :white_check_mark:

nate: taking over. I'll correlate customer-side errors and collect full logs (since sampling is now 100%). Also will snapshot metrics and attach to the incident tracker.

rca-bot: created incident record ID INC-2026-03-14-1764309876 and linked this thread. Recommended next steps: full RCA + postmortem within 72h.

marco.s: observability gaps identified (in-thread):
- log sampling change (10%) meant initial traces were sparse; we couldn't confirm root cause until sampling was increased
- dashboard mis-configured aggregation (avg vs p95) contributing to noisy alarms and delayed context
- lack of a quick-runbook command to temporarily ramp sampling for a service — we had to run manual config changes

liz: action items suggested:
- add a "ramp-sampling" runbook playbook in SRE runbooks (one-click to 100% for emergencies)
- lint dashboards for alarm-driving widgets to ensure p95/p99 appropriation for latency alarms
- add a pre-check to any kv-flush concurrency change requiring load-testing memory-profiles

priya.k: estimated customer impact: several live customers using predictive-gen saw elevated failure rates and retries for ~8-12 minutes. No data loss reported. Support notified with a short status note.

emily: posting a short status update to #customer-facing_incidents and adding follow-up in postmortem.

nate: attaching SQL/log snippets to the incident record and starting timeline doc. I'll ping when draft RCA ready for review.

priya.k: final note before handoff sleep: resolved for now, but we need a post-incident on-call deep-dive. Thanks all for quick response. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

rca-bot: postmortem template prefilled at /incidents/INC-2026-03-14-1764309876. Please add hypotheses, evidence, and mitigation/next steps.

ops-bot: audit log: pager acknowledged by priya.k at 1764309880, mitigation changes executed by ops-bot at 1764309945-1764309990.

nate: I'm keeping monitors muted for 15m while we validate, will update thread with any regression.

emily: noted. thanks team.
